note: Produbanco only: Banco Pichincha's site lists its cards without a tariff the request reached, Banco Guayaquil's home page links none and Banco del Pacífico's didn't answer. Produbanco's card tariffs (in force October 2026) and its card interest rates (in force from 2 October 2026), read in full: every personal Visa and Mastercard named in its table of reward-program and benefits-abroad charges (28 cards; the Visa Pyme and Visa Corporativa, business cards, aren't written). Maintaining a credit card costs nothing, and revolving consumer credit bears up to 16.77% a year effective, the Central Bank's ceiling for consumer credit, on every card. The reward-program and benefits-abroad charges (54 to 7 dollars before VAT, by the card's segment) don't state their period and aren't written; nor are the out-of-court collection charges, set by days overdue and the instalment's size, or the late-payment surcharge on the rate. No minimum payment, grace period or foreign transaction fee is stated. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) added Banco Bolivariano, whose Bankard cards it publishes terms for, chosen as one of the country's large banks that answered: its Bankard interest rates (an undated sheet on its transparency page, read 30 October 2026) give revolving credit at a nominal 15.60% a year, written as the rate on every card; its tariff of financial services for Banco Bolivariano and Bankard, October to December 2026 (read by eye: its figures are set in a font that doesn't extract as text), prices its personal cards by segment (Visa Infinite and MasterCard Black; Visa Signature and UnionPay Diamond; Visa and UnionPay Platinum; Visa, Mastercard and UnionPay Oro; Visa and Mastercard Clásica), each written: maintaining a card costs nothing; issuing a chip card for the first time costs 5.03 dollars with VAT, written as the issue fee (the renewal at the plastic's expiry, 5.03 too, isn't written); a domestic cheque returned costs 2.86 with VAT. As at Produbanco, the reward-plan and benefits-abroad charges state no period and aren't written; the cash advance fee is a fixed sum by the withdrawal's size (7.19 to 71.88 dollars), which the form's single share or sum doesn't hold, and isn't written; the card-abroad charge on purchases over 100 dollars (1.96) and the collection charges by days overdue aren't written; the Visa Empresarial CTA is a business card. No minimum payment, grace period or foreign transaction share is stated. Tried and not used: Banco Internacional's site refused the request (403), Diners Club del Ecuador's refused it too (403), Banco del Austro's and Banco del Pacífico's didn't answer, and Banco Guayaquil's pages answered 404 for its tariff.
